# A lockfile generated by a different npm major can pass that npm's clean install while failing the repository's declared package manager.

## Why

During Portal dependency maintenance, system npm 11.19.0 generated a lockfile
with `postcss-selector-parser@<7.1.6: 7.1.6` in overrides. Its clean install and
full Portal proof passed. The Portal declares npm 10.9.3; a clean install using
that exact version instead refused the lockfile with two missing
`postcss-selector-parser@6.1.4` entries. This is observed resolver compatibility,
not proof of a general defect in either npm major or in conditional overrides.

An unconditional exact `postcss-selector-parser: 7.1.6` override passed clean
installation under npm 10.9.3 without adding affected 6.x versions. The final
consumer and Portal proofs must follow that declared-version clean installation.
The linked Pull Request retains the failure and the corrected installation proof.

## How to apply

Read `packageManager` before regenerating or verifying a lockfile. Run its exact
npm version's `ci` after editing dependency declarations, then execute the owning
proof against that installed tree. Preserve a failed install and its diagnostics;
a successful install or build under another npm major cannot substitute for it.
Do not silence lock validation or restore vulnerable packages to satisfy it.

This first observation remains open: existing clean-install guidance does not
yet enforce the declared npm version, and shared installation/control-plane
changes require a separately scoped design rather than this dependency update.
